Log-linear model of the test profiles

Source: R/loglinear.R
loglinear.Rd

Defines a model in which the distribution of the response profiles is log-linear in each disease class, so the dependence between the tests is restricted to interactions of at most interaction_order tests. The object is passed to baysesp() as its model argument.

Usage

loglinear(
  interaction_order = 1L,
  prevalence_prior = prior_beta(0.5, 2),
  main_effects_prior = prior_normal(0, 1.5),
  interactions_prior = prior_normal(0, 1),
  verification = mar()
)

Arguments

interaction_order

A single whole number from 1 to the number of tests \(K\), the largest number of tests in an interaction. Default 1L (conditional independence). The lower bound is checked when the model is created; the upper bound is checked when the model is fitted.

prevalence_prior

Prior on the prevalence \(\pi\): a single prior, either on a probability, such as prior_beta(), which acts on \(\pi\), or on the real line, such as prior_normal(), which acts on \(\mathrm{logit}\,\pi\). Default prior_beta(0.5, 2), the uniform distribution on (0, 1).

main_effects_prior

A single prior on the real line, applied to each class-specific main effect \(\eta_{d,k}\) (one per test and disease class). Default prior_normal(0, 1.5). With order 1 these parameters are logits of sensitivities and of false positive rates.

interactions_prior

A single prior on the real line, applied to each class-specific interaction of order 2 or higher. Default prior_normal(0, 1). It has no effect when interaction_order = 1.

verification

The verification mechanism: mar() (default), with verification that depends only on the test profile, or mnar(), with verification that may also depend on the disease status.

Value

An object of class loglinear.

Details

Let \(K\) be the number of tests, \(t = (t_1, \dots, t_K)\) a response profile with \(t_k = 1\) for a positive result, \(d = 1\) for diseased and \(d = 0\) for healthy, and let \(m\) be interaction_order. For each disease class the profile probabilities \(\theta_d\) are $$\theta_d = \mathrm{softmax}(X_m \eta_d),$$ where \(X_m\) is the design matrix whose columns are the functions \(x_S(t) = \prod_{k \in S} t_k\), one for each set \(S\) of at most \(m\) tests, and \(\eta_d\) is the vector of the corresponding class-specific parameters \(\eta_{d,S}\). Equivalently, $$\theta_{d,t} \propto \exp\Big(\sum_{S} \eta_{d,S}\, x_S(t)\Big),$$ where the normalisation runs over all \(2^K\) profiles.

The order controls the structure of the dependence:

  • Order 1 (interaction_order = 1): the tests are conditionally independent given the disease status.

  • Order 2: each pair of tests may be associated within each class, but there are no interactions among three or more tests.

  • Order \(K\): no restriction, every profile distribution is allowed in each class.

The parameters have a direct interpretation. With order 1, \(\eta_{1,k} = \mathrm{logit}(Se_k)\) and \(\eta_{0,k} = \mathrm{logit}(1 - Sp_k)\), so the main effects are the logits of the sensitivity and of the false positive rate of test \(k\). A pairwise term \(\eta_{d,\{j,k\}}\) is the log odds ratio between tests \(j\) and \(k\) within class \(d\), given the results of the other tests (with order 2 it is the same whatever those results; with higher orders it is the value when the other tests are negative): zero means that the two tests are independent within that class, positive values mean that they are positively associated among the diseased (\(d = 1\)) or among the healthy (\(d = 0\)).

The log-likelihood of the data, with \(n_{t,d}\) verified subjects of profile \(t\) and disease status \(d\), \(u_t\) unverified subjects of profile \(t\), \(\pi_1 = \pi\) the prevalence and \(\pi_0 = 1 - \pi\), is $$\ell = \sum_t \Big[\sum_d n_{t,d} \log(\pi_d\,\theta_{d,t}\,\lambda_{t,d}) + u_t \log \sum_d \pi_d\,\theta_{d,t}\,(1 - \lambda_{t,d})\Big],$$ where \(\lambda_{t,d}\) is the probability of verification. With verification = mar() the verification probability does not depend on the disease status given the profile, so the verification term is separated from the disease model and can be ignored: $$\ell = \sum_t \Big[\sum_d n_{t,d} \log(\pi_d\,\theta_{d,t}) + u_t \log \sum_d \pi_d\,\theta_{d,t}\Big]$$ plus a term that depends only on the verification probabilities. With verification = mnar() the verification probability may depend on the disease status: $$\mathrm{logit}\,\lambda_{t,d} = \alpha_t + \beta d,$$ with one \(\alpha_t\) for each verified profile. The parameter \(\beta\) is the log odds ratio of verification between diseased and healthy subjects with the same profile, and \(\exp(-\beta)\) is the odds ratio of disease between unverified and verified subjects with the same profile. With verification = mnar(by_profile = TRUE) there is one \(\beta_t\) for each profile. Profiles that are never verified have \(\lambda_{t,d} = 0\).

With order lower than \(K\) the restricted structure also determines the disease proportion in the never-verified profiles, and makes \(\beta\) formally estimable. This information comes from the assumed structure, not from the data, and it is fragile if the structure is wrong. With order \(K\) the model imposes no restriction and \(\beta\) is not identified.

See also

saturated() for the model without restrictions on the profile distribution, mar() and mnar() for the verification mechanisms.

Examples

loglinear()                       # conditional independence
#> <loglinear> log-linear model of order 1
#>   prevalence_prior:   Beta(mean = 0.5, precision = 2)
#>   main_effects_prior: Normal(mean = 0, sd = 1.5)
#>   interactions_prior: Normal(mean = 0, sd = 1)
#>   verification:       mar
loglinear(interaction_order = 2)  # pairwise dependence
#> <loglinear> log-linear model of order 2
#>   prevalence_prior:   Beta(mean = 0.5, precision = 2)
#>   main_effects_prior: Normal(mean = 0, sd = 1.5)
#>   interactions_prior: Normal(mean = 0, sd = 1)
#>   verification:       mar
